narrative.text: The study is quiet. Outside, the last of the inaugural crowd is still dispersing from Republic Square. You can hear them faintly — music, voices, someone laughing. In here it is just you and Vyktor and a leather folder on the desk between you.
I waited until after the ball. You deserved one evening. But it is morning now and there are things you need to know before the Assembly session on Thursday.
He opens the folder. Does not hand it to you. Just opens it and begins.

The budget. Halvek left us a deficit of three hundred and forty million kroner. That is not a rounding error. That is structural. It was built over eleven years through a combination of state contracts awarded to party-connected firms, a pension freeze that was never disclosed publicly, and military procurement that bypassed the Finance Ministry entirely.
Three hundred and forty million. You knew the number. Seeing it in a folder, at this desk, in this chair — that is different.

Unemployment is at nineteen percent. The official figure is eleven. The gap is people who stopped being counted — seasonal workers, the informal economy, the foundry towns that were written off a decade ago. Kravenstal. Parts of Thornfeld. They exist in the real numbers but not the published ones.
He turns a page. His voice does not change. This is a man who has been carrying these numbers for months, waiting for someone to give them to.

Inflation is running at nine percent. The Central Bank has been holding the rate artificially low — Halvek's instruction, never formalized, never documented. The Bank Governor will want to correct it. When he does, borrowing costs go up. That affects the deficit. Everything connects to everything else.
You think about the speech you gave this morning. The hope in it. You meant every word. You still do. But hope does not close a three hundred and forty million kroner gap.

There is one more thing. Halvek left something in the palace archives — a set of files, sealed under his personal authority, that were never transferred to the incoming government through normal channels. My office found them this morning. I have not opened them. That decision belongs to you.
He places a second, smaller folder on top of the first. It has no label. Just a wax seal — Halvek's personal mark, a bird with closed wings.
Whatever is in there — it changes things. It always does. You can open it tonight, or you can give it to me and I will tell you what is in it when you are ready. Or —
You can leave it sealed. Some chancellors have. There is an argument for not knowing what you cannot yet act on.
The folder sits there. Small. Heavy in a way that has nothing to do with paper.

reactions.text: He nods once. No expression. 'I will leave you to it. I will be in my office.'

choices.text: Give them to Vyktor. Tell you what is in them when the time is right.

reactions.text: 'Understood.' He takes the folder. 'I will be careful with it.'

choices.text: Leave it sealed. You will deal with it when you are ready.

reactions.text: 'All right.' He closes the outer folder over it. 'It will be here when you want it.'

narrative.text: Vyktor leaves. The door closes. You sit alone with the folder and Halvek's wax seal.
The seal breaks cleanly. Inside — three documents, a photograph, and a handwritten note on Palace letterhead. You read for forty minutes. When you finish you sit very still for a long time.
You will not read them again tonight. But you will not forget what is in them either.

choices.text: Set the folder aside. Get some sleep.

narrative.text: Vyktor takes the folder. He does not open it here — just places it under his arm with the careful deliberateness of a man who handles dangerous things for a living.
I will read them tonight. I will tell you what you need to know and nothing more than that. Some things are easier to carry if you receive them in pieces.
You trust him. You have to. That is what it means to have a chief of staff.
The folder stays on the desk. Vyktor covers it with the budget report — out of sight, not out of existence.
There is no wrong answer here. Only different kinds of readiness.
You wonder, briefly, if that is true. Then you decide to believe it. For tonight.

choices.text: Leave the study. Get some sleep.
